design.decision: A nil bidder can always duck with a small card from another suit instead of being forced to win; a contract team can keep its honors in the led suit, or ruff with a low [♠].
design.opponent: Revealed the first time a partner plays a small card from another suit while holding the led suit; opponents' usual leads to bust a nil stop working, so they must attack through [♠].
design.rationale: A nil enabler worth buying before any payoff. It fixes the main way a nil fails, being forced to win with a high card in the led suit, and it still helps contracts. It uses the same hook as uc-trump-freely. The [2]-[5] filter keeps it from becoming a blanket any-suit rule, and the low [♠]s it includes give Low Cards a way to win by trumping.
design.draftText: Your team can play [2]s through [5]s even when it can follow suit
design.hooks: anySuit gains an optional card filter (`card`). With it, your team may play a matching card from another suit even when it can follow suit, on every trick, or only inside an existing first/last window when one is also given. Leading [♠] before [♠]s are broken stays illegal, and ordinary trump priority applies.

critic.concerns: A strong nil enabler that removes most bust-the-nil play; [2] through [5] is yet another low range, and [2] through [6] would match the pool.
